There are two basic reasons for role conflicts:

  1. The role is misunderstood
    • A person is not properly shown the duties and responsibilities of the role, or
    • People understand the role but choose to interpret it differently
  2. Society changes, so the role changes as well
    • constant change and rapid progress have contributed to a generation gap - differences in values and perspectives which lead to communication difficulties.

Mass media is another source of role conflict between parents, children and society.

HOW ROLE CHANGES CAN LEAD TO IMPROVEMENT

It is very common to find women employed outside the home.� Men are assuming more household chores than in the past.� On average, men generally do not want these changes as much as women, as they gain little in status by making these changes.� Women are pursuing high status careers, but fewer men are pursuing a position of full time homemaker.� This being said, many men are excellent cooks, domestic planners and have exceptional parenting skills.

The Female Advantage means that feminine qualities are bringing value to business management.� Women often manage people in a collaborative way  gaining ideas through consensus and compromise.


Role conflicts can arise because people are not willing or able to change.� When conflict leads to change, people are motivated to examine their roles carefully and seek ways to bring about change for the sake of growth.

Role conflicts can produce useful changes; they may cause us to examine our priorities and values.� They make may us more aware of injustices.� The result might be a breakdown of restricted and outdated habits that are not allowing people to progress and find their real areas of growth and achievement.
